source_text: Quoniam conatus omnimodae honestatis exstinguit, quoniam morum obscaenitatem operum Dei, id est naturae humanae, consolatur et auget infamia, quoniam omnia mandata legis reatui impossibilitatis id est iniquitatis addicit.
pass_a_gloss: Since it extinguishes attempts of every kind of honesty, since it consoles and increases the obscenity of manners by the infamy of the works of God, that is of human nature, since it binds all the commands of the law to the guilt of impossibility, that is of injustice.

lemmas.lexica: LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself
LS lex; Blaise lex Dei / sacred Law

pass_b_english: Because it extinguishes efforts toward every kind of honorable conduct; because it comforts and increases moral obscenity by defaming God’s works, that is, human nature; because it exposes all the law’s commands to the charge of demanding the impossible—that is, to the charge of injustice.

choices.why: Julian's charge against Augustine: treating evil as a nature rather than as will.
Julian means Scripture's legal/authoritative witness, especially the divine Law as teacher of justice.
rejected: natural law (unless the sentence is philosophical)

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
